I'm trying to resolve a naming mismatch: the header gkyl_gk_collisionless_flux_kernels.h declares multiblock-boundary kernel functions named like `gk_collisionless_flux_boundary_surfxmultib_boundary__lower_periodic_1x2v_ser_p1` (note: contains "multib_boundary__" - the word "boundary" appears twice total in the name), but the actual .c file gyrokinetic/ker/gk_collisionless_flux/gk_collisionless_flux_boundary_surfxmultib__1x2v_ser_p1.c defines functions named `gk_collisionless_flux_boundary_surfxmultib__lower_periodic_1x2v_ser_p1` (contains "multib__" only - "boundary" appears once).

Please search for:
1. Any Maxima/Lua/Python code-generation scripts in the repo (search directories like `maxima/`, `proto*/`, or grep for "multib_boundary" or "surfxmultib" as a naming template/string-building pattern in any .mac, .lua, .py generator scripts) that would reveal which naming convention is the "canonical"/intended one going forward.
2. Whether there are OTHER already-existing (older, already-wired-up and compiling) kernel functions anywhere in the repo that use a similar "X_boundary_Y__lower/upper_periodic/nonperiodic" naming pattern for a DIFFERENT physics module (not gk_collisionless_flux) - e.g. search other `ker/` subdirectories for "_lower_periodic_" or "_upper_nonperiodic_" naming patterns - to see if there's an established precedent elsewhere in the codebase for how multiblock+periodic boundary kernel names are supposed to be constructed. This would tell us which of the two spellings matches existing codebase conventions.
3. Check git blame / git log for gyrokinetic/ker/gk_collisionless_flux/gkyl_gk_collisionless_flux_kernels.h to see the most recent commit that touched it and whether that commit (or its message) mentions the naming scheme or was authored by a code-gen script (i.e., is this header committed/generated by tooling not present in the working tree, or is it hand-maintained).

Report back concisely with file paths and the exact naming pattern found, and state clearly which spelling ("multib_boundary__" vs "multib__") appears to be the established/canonical one, if determinable. This is read-only research - do not edit anything.
